decisions.choice: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet: a psalm, with a title like those of the Psalms
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 is a psalm. It has a title naming its author and the kind of song (as Psalm 7:1), "Selah" three times (verses 3, 9, 13), and a closing note for the music director (verse 19), like the titles of Psalm 4:1 and others. Psalms 17, 86, 90 and 102 are also called "prayers". It was evidently used in worship. The prophet answers God's word in chapter 2 with praise and trust.

decisions.choice: on shigionoth: a musical term whose sense is unknown
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "shiggaion", the term in the title of Psalm 7, and is used only here. It names a kind of song or a tune; some link it with a verb for wandering or reeling, others with a word for lament. "On" may mean "set to" or "in the style of".

decisions.choice: shigionoth (L, B); to be sung as a song (R)
decisions.reason: As "shiggaion" in Psalm 7:1, Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew word, and Readable says only that it is a song, since the exact sense is unknown (m2). The title is its own verse and stays as one line.

decisions.choice: "sobre sigionot" (L, B); "Canto" (R)
decisions.reason: The musical term is transliterated at L and B, as Psalm 7:1 "Sigayón" in Spanish; R gives "Canto", as the Spanish psalm titles do. The chapter's titles and "Selah" follow the Spanish Psalms.

decisions.choice: "sur le mode des shiguionoth" (L, B); "à chanter comme un chant" (R)
decisions.reason: The musical term is transliterated as the French Psalm 7:1 "shiggayon" is, in the French spelling with "gu"; Readable says only that it is sung, as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: The prayer speaks to God with "tu"; the past events of verses 3-15 are in the passé composé (and imparfait), as the Psalms, never the passé simple
decisions.reason: Habakkuk 3 is a psalm, that is, speech, not narrative (the terms for these books).

decisions.choice: "kwa shigionothi" (L, B); "ya kuimbwa kama wimbo" (R)
decisions.reason: Habakkuk 3 follows the psalm titles: the musical term is transliterated, as Psalm 7:1 "Shigayoni", with "wimbo" at Readable. "Sela" stays at the end of the verse, as in the published Psalms.

decisions.choice: "theo điệu Si-ga-giốt" (L, B) / "để hát như một bài ca" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note: the musical term is transliterated as in Psalm 7:1 ("Si-ga-giôn"), in its plural form; Readable says only that it is a song, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: *shigionoth* is "시기오놋" (L, B) and "노래" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording (uncertain spelling): a musical term whose sense is unknown, transliterated as the psalm titles are; Readable says "노래" as Psalm 7:1 R does.

decisions.choice: The prayer follows each verse's turn: to God in 합쇼체 with "주님" and "저" (3:2, 8–15), about God in the plain style with -시- and "그분" (3:3–7, 16–19)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet says for Habakkuk 3 and Jonah 2, and as the Korean Psalms do (Psalm 23): the Hebrew moves between speaking to God and speaking about him.

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh, I have heard your report; I fear. Yahweh, your work, in [the] midst of years revive it; in [the] midst of years make [it] known; in wrath, to have compassion remember.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have heard the report of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; I am afraid. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work, in the midst of [the] years revive it; \q in the midst of [the] years make [it] known; \q in rage remember to have compassion.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have heard of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fame, and I stand in awe. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, renew {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work in our own time; \q in our own time make it known; \q in wrath, remember mercy.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I have heard about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done, and I am filled with awe. \q {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do those great things again in our time. \q Let people see them in our day. \q Even when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry, remember to show mercy.

decisions.choice: I have heard the report of you; I am afraid: awe at what God has done
decisions.reason: "Report" is what Habakkuk has heard of the LORD: his deeds in the past, such as the exodus (verses 3-15), and his word in chapter 2. "I am afraid" is the trembling awe of one who knows God's power (verse 16).

decisions.choice: in the midst of the years: in our own time
decisions.reason: Habakkuk asks God to do again, in his own day, the mighty work he did in the past, rather than leaving it in history. "Revive it" means bring it to life again.

decisions.choice: in wrath remember mercy
decisions.reason: The word for "mercy" is the tender compassion of a parent (Psalm 103:13). Habakkuk accepts that judgment is coming (1:12; 3:16) and asks that God's anger be tempered with compassion for his people.

decisions.choice: fame (B); what you have done (R); renew, in our own time (B); do those great things again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "report" was (m1) and what "in the midst of the years" means (m2).

decisions.choice: "souviens-toi d'avoir compassion" (L); "n'oublie pas la compassion" (B), "n'oublie pas d'avoir pitié" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the tender compassion of a parent (m3); Balanced and Readable turn "remember" into the plainer "do not forget".

decisions.choice: "huruma" for *racham*; "sifa zako" (L, B) for the "report" of God
decisions.reason: *Rachamim* is "huruma" in these books; "sifa" (fame) says what the report was (m1), and the line is drafted away from the familiar wording.

decisions.choice: "in wrath remember mercy": "진노하실 때에도 불쌍히 여기심을 기억하십시오" (L), "긍휼을 잊지 마십시오" (B), "자비를 베푸시는 것을 기억해 주십시오" (R)
decisions.reason: *Rachem* is "불쌍히 여기다" and the noun "긍휼" (L, B) and "자비" (R), as the term sheet sets; the familiar older wording with -옵소서 is avoided.

decisions.choice: "compasión"
decisions.reason: The verb is the one of tender compassion (raham); the Spanish uses "compasión" at every level, kept apart from hesed ("amor leal" / "amor fiel").

decisions.choice: the prayer of chapter 3 says "tôi", as the Psalms do, with God as "Ngài"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision at 3:1: the chapter is a psalm with a psalm's title and notes; the Vietnamese Psalms have the psalmist say "tôi" to God (style guide 7a), so the psalm keeps that rather than the "con" of Habakkuk's complaints in 1:2-17.

decisions.choice: God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran: as when he came from Sinai
decisions.reason: Teman is a region of Edom, south of Judah (Jeremiah 49:7; Obadiah 9), and Paran the wilderness between Sinai and Canaan (Numbers 10:12). Older poems picture the LORD marching from the south, from Sinai, Seir and Paran, to help his people (Deuteronomy 33:2; Judges 5:4; Psalm 68:8-9). Habakkuk recalls that coming in verses 3-15. The word for "God" here is a rare, poetic form.

decisions.choice: came: the poem tells what God did, in the language of vision
alternatives: God comes: a vision of a future coming
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs of verses 3-15 shift between forms that can be past, present or future. The poem recalls God's coming at the exodus and Sinai, and pictures it as if seen anew; Habakkuk hopes to see the same again (verse 2). The translation tells it as past.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in this chapter (verses 3, 9 and 13). It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude. It is not part of what is said.

decisions.choice: Selah moved to the end
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Selah in the middle of the verse, after the first line. Every level puts it at the end so that the verse reads as a whole, as in Psalm 57:4.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (m3), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

decisions.choice: "Selah" at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: Selah stands mid-verse in the Hebrew; as in the Spanish Psalms it is moved to the end of the verse's last line and kept as it is at every level.

decisions.choice: God's coming (3:3-15) told in the passé composé at every level, with the imparfait for description
alternatives: passé simple at L and B
decisions.reason: Habakkuk 3 is a prayer, so its account of what God did is speech, as Jonah's psalm and the Psalms in French; the term sheet names this chapter.

decisions.choice: "Sela" at the end of the verse, kept as it is at every level
decisions.reason: A word whose meaning is unknown, probably a musical direction (m3); as in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: "Sê-la" at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: As the published Psalms do with a mid-verse Selah, and as the English moves it.

decisions.choice: "셀라" stands at the end of the verse, as the English moves it, and is kept at every level
alternatives: "셀라" in the middle of the verse
decisions.reason: As the Korean Psalms (3:3) and the term sheet: the word's meaning is unknown and Readable does not explain it away; a mid-verse Selah moves to the end of the verse's last line (Psalm 57:4). Teman is "데만" and Paran "바란", as published.

decisions.choice: "Su esplendor" at the start of a line
decisions.reason: A line that begins with God's possessive is capitalized at both options, so it carries no deity_pronoun span, as the English does.

source.text: וְנֹ֨גַהּ֙ כָּא֣וֹר תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה קַרְנַ֥יִם מִיָּד֖וֹ ל֑וֹ וְשָׁ֖ם חֶבְי֥וֹן עֻזֹּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And brightness like the light was; two horns from his hand [belong] to him; and there [was the] hiding of his power.

en.L: And [his] brightness was like the light; \q rays [came] from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q and there {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power was hidden.
en.B: His brightness was like the sunlight; \q rays flashed from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q and there {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power lay hidden.
en.R: He was as bright as the sun. \q Rays of light came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q where {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power was hidden.

es.L: Y [su] resplandor era como la luz; \q rayos [salían] de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano, \q y allí se escondía {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder.
es.B: Su resplandor era como la luz del sol; \q de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano brotaban rayos, \q y allí estaba escondido {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder.
es.R: Brillaba como el sol. \q De {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano salían rayos de luz, \q donde estaba escondido {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} poder.

fr.L: Et [{{deity_pronoun:son|Son}}] éclat était comme la lumière ; \q des rayons [sortaient] de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main, \q et là {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance était cachée.
fr.B: Son éclat était comme la lumière du soleil ; \q des rayons jaillissaient de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main, \q et là se cachait {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance.
fr.R: Il brillait comme le soleil. \q Des rayons de lumière sortaient de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main, \q où {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} puissance était cachée.

sw.L: Na mng'ao [wake] ulikuwa kama nuru; \q mionzi [ilitoka] mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, \q na hapo nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zilifichwa.
sw.B: Mng'ao {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulikuwa kama mwanga wa jua; \q mionzi ilimetameta kutoka mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, \q na hapo nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zilikuwa zimefichwa.
sw.R: Alikuwa anang'aa kama jua. \q Mionzi ya nuru ilitoka mkononi {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, \q mahali ambapo nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zilifichwa.

vi.L: Và [sự] chói sáng [của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] như ánh sáng; \q tia sáng [phát ra] từ tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và tại đó quyền năng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được giấu kín.
vi.B: Sự chói sáng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như ánh mặt trời; \q tia sáng lóe ra từ tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và quyền năng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ẩn giấu ở đó.
vi.R: Ngài sáng chói như mặt trời. \q Những tia sáng phát ra từ tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q nơi quyền năng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được giấu kín.

ko.L: [그분의] 광채가 빛과 같고, \q 그분의 손에서 광선들이 [나오며], \q 그곳에 그분의 능력이 숨겨져 있었다.
ko.B: 그분의 광채는 햇빛 같았고, \q 그분의 손에서 빛줄기가 뻗어 나왔다. \q 그곳에 그분의 능력이 감추어져 있었다.
ko.R: 그분께서는 해처럼 밝게 빛나셨다. \q 그분의 손에서 빛줄기가 뻗어 나왔다. \q 그 손에 그분의 능력이 숨겨져 있었다.

decisions.choice: rays from his hand
decisions.reason: The word usually means "horns". The related verb is used of Moses' face shining with rays of light (Exodus 34:29), so here it is rays of light, like lightning, flashing from God's hand. "Horns" are also a picture of strength (Psalm 18:3).

decisions.choice: there his power was hidden
decisions.reason: The light that shone from God was only the covering of a power greater still, which no one can see (Exodus 33:20-23; Psalm 18:12).

decisions.choice: [his] brightness (L); sunlight (B); as bright as the sun (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "brightness" without "his"; Literal brackets it. The light is the light of day, the sun, as Balanced and Readable say.

decisions.choice: "rayos" for the word usually meaning "horns"
decisions.reason: Rays of light, as the verb for Moses' shining face (m1).

decisions.choice: "des rayons" for the word usually meaning "horns"
decisions.reason: The word is used of rays of light here, as the verb for Moses' shining face (m1).

decisions.choice: "mionzi" for the word usually meaning "horns"
decisions.reason: Rays of light, as the verb for Moses' shining face (m1).

decisions.choice: "tia sáng" for the word usually meaning "horns"
decisions.reason: Rays of light, as the verb for Moses' shining face (m1).

decisions.choice: "광선" (L, B), "빛줄기" (R) for the word usually meaning "horns"
decisions.reason: Rays of light, as the verb for Moses' shining face (m1).

source.text: לְפָנָ֖יו יֵ֣לֶךְ דָּ֑בֶר וְיֵצֵ֥א רֶ֖שֶׁף לְרַגְלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Before him went pestilence, and plague went out at his feet.

en.L: Before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went pestilence, \q and plague went out at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.
en.B: Disease went ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and plague followed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heels.
en.R: Disease went ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and plague followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} iba la pestilencia, \q y la plaga salía a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies.
es.B: La enfermedad iba delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q y la plaga {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} seguía los pasos.
es.R: La enfermedad iba delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \q y la plaga iba detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} marchait la peste, \q et le fléau sortait sur {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pas.
fr.B: La maladie marchait devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q et le fléau suivait sur {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} talons.
fr.R: La maladie marchait devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \q et le fléau {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivait.

sw.L: Mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilienda tauni, \q na pigo lilitoka miguuni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.
sw.B: Ugonjwa ulimtangulia, \q na pigo lilifuata nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

vi.L: Ôn dịch đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và dịch lệ theo sau chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Bệnh dịch đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và tai ương theo sát gót {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Bệnh tật đi trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và dịch bệnh theo sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그분 앞에서는 역병이 가고, \q 그분의 발에서는 전염병이 나갔다.
ko.B: 질병이 그분 앞에서 나아가고, \q 전염병이 그분의 발꿈치를 뒤따랐다.
ko.R: 질병이 그분보다 앞서 갔고, \q 전염병이 그분을 뒤따랐다.

decisions.choice: pestilence and plague: attendants of the divine warrior
decisions.reason: Pestilence and plague are pictured as servants who go before and behind a king (Psalm 78:48-50; Deuteronomy 32:24). The second word is also the name of a god of plague worshiped by Israel's neighbors; here plague is no god but the LORD's servant. The plagues of Egypt may be in mind (Exodus 9:3, 15).

decisions.choice: Disease (B, R); at his heels (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "disease" for the older "pestilence". "At his feet" means close behind him, at his heels.

source.text: עָמַ֣ד׀וַיְמֹ֣דֶד אֶ֗רֶץ רָאָה֙ וַיַּתֵּ֣ר גּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּתְפֹּֽצְצוּ֙ הַרְרֵי־עַ֔ד שַׁח֖וּ גִּבְע֣וֹת עוֹלָ֑ם הֲלִיכ֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: He stood and shook [the] earth; he looked and made nations leap; and [the] mountains of antiquity were shattered; [the] hills of antiquity bowed down; [the] goings of antiquity [belong] to him.

en.L: He stood and shook [the] earth; he saw and made [the] nations leap; \q and the age-old mountains were shattered; \q the everlasting hills sank low; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways [are] everlasting.
en.B: He stood, and the earth shook; he looked, and the nations trembled. \q The ancient mountains broke apart; \q the age-old hills sank down. \q His ways are eternal.
en.R: He stood up and made the earth shake. He looked, and the nations trembled. \q The mountains that had stood for ages broke apart. \q The ancient hills sank down. \q His ways are eternal.

es.L: Se detuvo y sacudió [la] tierra; miró e hizo saltar a [las] naciones; \q y los montes antiguos se hicieron pedazos; \q las colinas eternas se hundieron; \q {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} caminos [son] eternos.
es.B: Se detuvo, y la tierra tembló; miró, y las naciones se estremecieron. \q Los montes antiguos se partieron; \q las colinas de siempre se hundieron. \q Sus caminos son eternos.
es.R: Se puso de pie e hizo temblar la tierra. Miró, y las naciones se estremecieron. \q Los montes que estaban allí desde siempre se partieron. \q Las colinas antiguas se hundieron. \q Sus caminos son eternos.

fr.L: Il {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est dressé et a ébranlé la terre ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a regardé et a fait sursauter les nations ; \q et les montagnes antiques ont volé en éclats ; \q les collines éternelles se sont affaissées ; \q {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} chemins [sont] éternels.
fr.B: Il {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est dressé, et la terre a tremblé ; il a regardé, et les nations ont frémi. \q Les montagnes anciennes se sont brisées ; \q les collines d’autrefois se sont affaissées. \q Ses chemins sont éternels.
fr.R: Il {{deity_pronoun:s’|S’}}est levé et a fait trembler la terre. Il a regardé, et les nations ont tremblé. \q Les montagnes qui étaient là depuis toujours se sont brisées. \q Les vieilles collines se sont effondrées. \q Ses chemins sont éternels.

sw.L: Alisimama akaitetemesha nchi; alitazama akayafanya mataifa kuruka; \q na milima ya kale ilivunjwavunjwa; \q vilima vya milele viliinama; \q njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} [ni] za milele.
sw.B: Alisimama, na dunia ikatetemeka; alitazama, na mataifa yakatetemeka. \q Milima ya kale ilipasuka; \q vilima vya zamani vilizama chini. \q Njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} ni za milele.
sw.R: Alisimama, akaifanya dunia itetemeke. Alitazama, na mataifa yakatetemeka. \q Milima iliyokuwa imesimama tangu zamani ilipasuka. \q Vilima vya kale vilizama chini. \q Njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} ni za milele.

vi.L: Ngài đứng và làm rung chuyển đất; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn và làm các nước nhảy dựng; \q và các núi đời xưa bị vỡ tan; \q các đồi đời đời sụp xuống; \q đường lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] đời đời.
vi.B: Ngài đứng lên, và đất rung chuyển; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn, và các nước run rẩy. \q Các núi cổ xưa vỡ tan; \q các đồi lâu đời lún xuống. \q Đường lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn đến đời đời.
vi.R: Ngài đứng dậy và làm cho đất rung chuyển. Ngài nhìn, và các nước run sợ. \q Những ngọn núi đã đứng vững từ bao đời vỡ ra từng mảnh. \q Những ngọn đồi cổ xưa lún xuống. \q Đường lối {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn mãi mãi.

ko.L: 그분께서 서시어 땅을 흔드시고, 보시어 민족들을 뛰게 하셨다. \q 영원한 산들이 부서지고, \q 오래된 언덕들이 내려앉았다. \q 그분의 길들은 영원하다.
ko.B: 그분께서 서시니 땅이 흔들리고, 그분께서 보시니 민족들이 떨었다. \q 옛 산들이 갈라지고, \q 오래된 언덕들이 주저앉았다. \q 그분의 길은 영원하다.
ko.R: 그분께서 일어서시자 땅이 흔들렸다. 그분께서 바라보시자 민족들이 떨었다. \q 오랜 세월 서 있던 산들이 갈라졌다. \q 오래된 언덕들이 내려앉았다. \q 그분의 길은 영원하다.

decisions.choice: shook the earth
alternatives: he stood and measured the earth
decisions.reason: The verb may come from a root meaning "measure" (he stood and measured the earth) or from one meaning "shake". The shaking of the earth fits the next lines.

decisions.choice: the age-old mountains ... the everlasting hills: what seems most permanent gives way
decisions.reason: The mountains and hills are called ancient and everlasting because nothing in the world seems more lasting (Genesis 49:26; Deuteronomy 33:15). They break and sink before the eternal God.

decisions.choice: his ways are everlasting
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that his ways are eternal, or that the ancient paths, the roads he walked when he came from Sinai, are his.

decisions.choice: the earth shook ... the nations trembled (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what happened when he stood and looked; "made the nations leap" means made them start up in fear.

source.text: תַּ֣חַת אָ֔וֶן רָאִ֖יתִי אָהֳלֵ֣י כוּשָׁ֑ן יִרְגְּז֕וּן יְרִיע֖וֹת אֶ֥רֶץ מִדְיָֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Under trouble I saw [the] tents of Cushan; trembled [the] tent curtains of [the] land of Midian.

en.L: Under distress I saw the tents of Cushan; \q the tent curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
en.B: I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; \q the tent curtains of Midian shook.
en.R: I saw the people of Cushan in their tents, full of fear. \q The people of Midian trembled in their tents.

es.L: Bajo aflicción vi las tiendas de Cusán; \q temblaban las cortinas de las tiendas de la tierra de Madián.
es.B: Vi las tiendas de Cusán en angustia; \q las cortinas de las tiendas de Madián se estremecieron.
es.R: Vi a la gente de Cusán en sus tiendas, llena de miedo. \q La gente de Madián temblaba en sus tiendas.

fr.L: Sous la détresse j’ai vu les tentes de Koushân ; \q les toiles de tente du pays de Madian ont tremblé.
fr.B: J’ai vu les tentes de Koushân dans l’angoisse ; \q les toiles des tentes de Madian ont frémi.
fr.R: J’ai vu les gens de Koushân dans leurs tentes, remplis de peur. \q Les gens de Madian tremblaient dans leurs tentes.

sw.L: Niliona hema za Kushani zikiwa katika taabu; \q mapazia ya hema za nchi ya Midiani yalitetemeka.
sw.B: Niliona hema za Kushani zikiwa katika dhiki; \q mapazia ya hema za Midiani yalitikisika.
sw.R: Niliona watu wa Kushani katika hema zao, wakiwa wamejaa hofu. \q Watu wa Midiani walitetemeka ndani ya hema zao.

vi.L: Tôi thấy các trại của Cu-san trong cơn khốn đốn; \q màn trại của xứ Ma-đi-an run rẩy.
vi.B: Tôi thấy các lều trại Cu-san lâm cảnh khốn cùng; \q màn trại của Ma-đi-an run rẩy.
vi.R: Tôi thấy dân Cu-san trong lều trại của họ đầy sợ hãi. \q Dân Ma-đi-an run rẩy trong lều của mình.

ko.L: 재난 아래 있는 구산의 장막들을 내가 보았다. \q 미디안 땅의 휘장들이 떨었다.
ko.B: 나는 구산의 장막들이 고통에 빠진 것을 보았다. \q 미디안의 장막 휘장들이 흔들렸다.
ko.R: 나는 구산 사람들이 장막 안에서 두려워 떠는 것을 보았다. \q 미디안 사람들도 장막 안에서 떨었다.

decisions.choice: Cushan and Midian: desert peoples on the route from Sinai
decisions.reason: Midian lay east and south of Edom, in the region where Moses had lived (Exodus 2:15; 3:1). Cushan is named only here; it is set beside Midian and was probably a people of the same region (compare Numbers 12:1, where Moses' wife, a Midianite, may be called a Cushite). The tribes along God's route tremble as he passes.

decisions.choice: I saw: the prophet sees the vision
decisions.reason: Habakkuk speaks as one who sees God's coming before his eyes.

decisions.choice: the people of Cushan in their tents; The people of Midian (R)
decisions.reason: The tents and tent curtains stand for the people who live in them; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: "Koushân", "Madian"
decisions.reason: Cushan is otherwise unknown; French spells it as the published "Koush" names; Midian keeps the published Pentateuch's usual "Madian".

decisions.choice: "Kushani", kept apart from Cush ("Kushi")
decisions.reason: Cushan is named only here (m1); the form follows the usual Swahili pattern for a new name.

decisions.choice: "tôi" for Habakkuk seeing the vision; "Cu-san", as Judges 3:8
decisions.reason: Here he speaks about what he saw, not to God (m2).

decisions.choice: "Cusán", "Madián"
decisions.reason: "Madián" is the published Spanish form; "Cusán" follows it in shape (also Judges 3:8 "Cusán-risataim").

decisions.choice: Cushan is "구산" and Midian "미디안"
decisions.reason: Cushan is a desert people near Midian, not Cush ("구스"); "구산" gives the Hebrew form and keeps them apart. Midian is spelled as published.

source.text: הֲבִנְהָרִים֙ חָרָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה אִ֤ם בַּנְּהָרִים֙ אַפֶּ֔ךָ אִם־בַּיָּ֖ם עֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י תִרְכַּב֙ עַל־סוּסֶ֔יךָ מַרְכְּבֹתֶ֖יךָ יְשׁוּעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Was it against rivers [that] it burned, Yahweh? Or [is] against the rivers your anger, or against the sea your fury, that you ride on your horses, your chariots of salvation?

en.L: Was it against [the] rivers [that anger] burned, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? \q Or [was] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger against the rivers, \q or {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury against the sea, \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rode on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chariots of salvation?
en.B: Was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger burning against the rivers, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}? \q Was {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath against the streams, \q or {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury against the sea, \q as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rode {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chariots of salvation?
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, were {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} angry with the rivers? \q Were {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} angry with the streams? \q Were {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} furious with the sea \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rode on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses \q and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chariots to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people?

es.L: ¿Contra [los] ríos ardió [la ira], {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}? \q ¿O [fue] contra los ríos {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira, \q o contra el mar {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} furor, \q cuando montaste sobre {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caballos, \q {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} carros de salvación?
es.B: ¿Ardía {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira contra los ríos, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}? \q ¿Estaba {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enojo contra las corrientes, \q o {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} furor contra el mar, \q cuando montabas {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caballos, \q {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} carros de salvación?
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿estabas enojado con los ríos? \q ¿Estabas enojado con las corrientes? \q ¿Estabas furioso con el mar \q cuando cabalgabas en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caballos \q y en {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} carros para salvar a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo?

fr.L: Est-ce contre les fleuves [que la colère] s’est enflammée, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? \q Ou {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère [était-elle] contre les fleuves, \q ou {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fureur contre la mer, \q quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} montais sur {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chevaux, \q {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chars de salut ?
fr.B: Est-ce contre les fleuves que brûlait {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ? \q Ton courroux était-il contre les rivières, \q ou {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fureur contre la mer, \q quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} montais {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chevaux, \q {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chars de salut ?
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, étais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} en colère contre les fleuves ? \q Étais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} en colère contre les rivières ? \q Étais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} furieux contre la mer \q quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} montais {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chevaux \q et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chars pour sauver {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple ?

sw.L: Je, ilikuwa dhidi ya mito [hasira yako] iliwaka, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? \q Au hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} [ilikuwa] dhidi ya mito, \q au ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} dhidi ya bahari, \q ulipopanda farasi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q magari {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya wokovu?
sw.B: Je, hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ilikuwa ikiwaka dhidi ya mito, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? \q Je, ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ilikuwa dhidi ya vijito, \q au hasira kali {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} dhidi ya bahari, \q ulipopanda farasi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q magari {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya wokovu?
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, je, uliikasirikia mito? \q Je, uliikasirikia mikondo ya maji? \q Je, uliikasirikia bahari \q ulipopanda farasi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} \q na magari {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ya vita ili kuwaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}?

vi.L: Có phải [cơn giận] bừng cháy nghịch cùng các sông chăng, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? \q Hay cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [nghịch cùng] các sông, \q hay cơn thịnh nộ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghịch cùng biển, \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cưỡi trên các ngựa của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q các xe chiến mã cứu rỗi của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, có phải cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bừng lên nghịch cùng các sông? \q Có phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận với các dòng nước, \q hay nổi thịnh nộ với biển cả, \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cưỡi ngựa của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q những xe chiến mã đem lại sự cứu rỗi?
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, có phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giận các con sông? \q Có phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giận các dòng suối? \q Có phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận với biển \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cưỡi ngựa \q và đi trên các xe chiến mã của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để giải cứu dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 강들을 향하여 [진노가] 타올랐습니까? \q 주님의 진노가 강들을 향한 것이었습니까? \q 주님의 격노가 바다를 향한 것이었습니까? \q 주님께서 주님의 말들을, \q 주님의 구원의 병거들을 타실 때에 말입니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 강들을 향해 진노하셨습니까? \q 주님의 분노가 시내들을 향한 것이었습니까? \q 주님의 격노가 바다를 향한 것이었습니까? \q 주님께서 말을 타고, \q 구원의 병거를 몰고 오실 때에 말입니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 강들에게 화가 나셨습니까? \q 시내들에게 화가 나셨습니까? \q 바다에게 분노하셨습니까? \q 그래서 주님께서 말을 타시고 \q 병거를 몰고 오셔서 주님의 백성을 구하셨습니까?

decisions.choice: the rivers and the sea: the Red Sea and the Jordan
decisions.reason: The questions recall how the sea fled and the Jordan turned back before the LORD when he brought Israel out of Egypt and into the land (Exodus 14-15; Joshua 3; Psalm 114:3-5). The poem also uses the old picture of the sea and rivers as powers of chaos that God subdues (Psalm 74:13-14; 93:3-4). The answer to the questions is no: his anger was against his people's enemies (verses 12-13).

decisions.choice: you rode on your horses, your chariots of salvation: God as a warrior
decisions.reason: The LORD is pictured as a warrior in a chariot, riding the clouds and storm to rescue his people (Deuteronomy 33:26; Psalm 18:11; 68:5).

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue and victory
decisions.reason: The word is rescue from enemies, which is also victory over them; it returns in verses 13 and 18.

decisions.choice: the vocative LORD with no "O"; [that anger] (L); your anger (B); angry (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Psalms, the LORD is addressed without "O". The Hebrew says only "Did it burn", which is said of anger; Literal brackets the word.

decisions.choice: The vocative "{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}" with no « ô »; the prayer turns to God as "tu" again from here to verse 15
decisions.reason: As the Psalms; the poem now speaks to God directly.

decisions.choice: From here to verse 15 the prayer speaks to God in 합쇼체 ("주님께서 … 타실 때에")
decisions.reason: The poem turns from speaking about God (3-7) to speaking to him; the speech level follows the turn, as in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: "[hasira yako]" (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "burned" has no stated subject; Swahili needs one, supplied in brackets, so the free possessive "yako" sits inside the brackets without a span.

decisions.choice: "sự cứu rỗi" (L, B) / "giải cứu" (R) for salvation
decisions.reason: The Isaiah terms note's wording: "sự cứu rỗi" (L, B) / the verb "cứu" or "giải cứu" (R).

en.L: Your bow was laid bare; \q [the] arrows [were] sworn [by] a word. \q With rivers {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} split [the] earth. Selah
en.B: Your bow was drawn from its case; \q the arrows were charged by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word. \q You split the earth with rivers. Selah

vi.L: Cây cung của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được để trần ra; \q [các mũi tên được] thề [bởi] lời. \q Ngài dùng các sông xẻ đất ra. Sê-la

ko.B: 주님께서 활을 집에서 꺼내시고, \q 주님의 말씀으로 화살들에게 명령하셨습니다. \q 주님께서 강들로 땅을 가르셨습니다. 셀라
ko.R: 주님께서 활을 꺼내 드시고 \q 화살들에게 날아가라고 명령하셨습니다. \q 주님께서 땅을 쪼개시자 강물이 흘러나왔습니다. 셀라

decisions.choice: [the] arrows [were] sworn [by] a word: a very obscure line
alternatives: you filled your quiver with arrows
the oaths to the tribes were a sure word
decisions.reason: The middle line is three nouns: "oaths" (or "sated" or "sevens"), "rods" (which can mean arrows, staffs or tribes) and "word" (or "command"). It is one of the hardest lines in the Bible to understand. It is taken here to mean that God's arrows were sent out under his command, as if sworn to their task. Other readings are "the rods of chastisement were sworn by your word", "you filled your quiver with arrows", and "oaths were sworn to the tribes". The sense of the verse as a whole is clear: God takes up his weapons.

decisions.choice: with rivers you split the earth
decisions.reason: The earth was split as water burst out, perhaps recalling water from the rock in the wilderness (Exodus 17:6; Psalm 78:15-16) or the opening of springs and rivers in the storm (Psalm 74:15).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in this chapter (verses 3, 9 and 13). It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude. It is not part of what is said.

decisions.choice: Selah moved to the end
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Selah after the second line. Every level puts it at the end of the verse, as in verse 3, and keeps the word as it is (see verse 3).

decisions.choice: drawn from its case (B); took out your bow (R); charged by your word, commanded your arrows (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Laid bare" means taken from its cover, ready for use. Balanced and Readable follow the reading in m1.

decisions.reason: A very obscure line (m1); Literal follows the English reading with the supplied words in brackets.

decisions.choice: "les flèches [ont été] liées par serment [par] une parole" (L), marked uncertain
alternatives: les verges de châtiment ont été jurées
decisions.reason: One of the hardest lines in the Bible (m1); Literal follows the reading the English takes, with every supplied word in brackets.

decisions.reason: A very obscure line (m1); Literal follows the English reading with the supplied words in brackets.

records.literal_gloss: They saw you; they writhe, mountains; a downpour of water passed over; gave the deep its voice; [on] high its hands it lifted.

en.L: [The] mountains saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; they writhed; \q a downpour of water passed by; \q the deep gave its voice; \q it lifted its hands on high.
en.B: The mountains saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and writhed; \q a torrent of water swept past; \q the deep roared aloud \q and lifted its hands high.
en.R: When the mountains saw {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, they shook. \q Floods of water rushed by. \q The deep ocean roared \q and raised its waves high.

es.L: [Los] montes {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} vieron; se retorcieron; \q un aguacero de aguas pasó; \q el abismo dio su voz; \q en lo alto alzó sus manos.
es.B: Los montes {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} vieron y se retorcieron; \q pasó un torrente de aguas; \q el abismo rugió con fuerza \q y alzó en alto sus manos.
es.R: Cuando los montes {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} vieron, temblaron. \q Pasaron grandes inundaciones. \q El océano profundo rugió \q y levantó en alto sus olas.

fr.L: Les montagnes {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont vu ; elles se sont tordues ; \q une averse d’eaux est passée ; \q l’abîme a fait entendre sa voix ; \q il a levé ses mains en haut.
fr.B: Les montagnes {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont vu et se sont tordues de douleur ; \q un torrent d’eau a déferlé ; \q l’abîme a rugi \q et a levé les mains bien haut.
fr.R: Quand les montagnes {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont vu, elles ont tremblé. \q Des flots d’eau se sont précipités. \q L’océan profond a rugi \q et a soulevé ses vagues très haut.

sw.L: Milima ilikuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}; iligaagaa kwa uchungu; \q mafuriko ya maji yalipita; \q kilindi kilitoa sauti yake; \q kiliinua mikono yake juu.
sw.B: Milima ilikuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ikagaagaa kwa uchungu; \q mafuriko ya maji yalipita kwa nguvu; \q kilindi kilinguruma kwa sauti kuu \q na kuinua mikono yake juu.
sw.R: Milima ilipokuona {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, ilitetemeka. \q Mafuriko ya maji yalipita kwa kasi. \q Bahari yenye kina ilinguruma \q na kuinua mawimbi yake juu.

vi.L: Các núi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; chúng quằn quại; \q một trận mưa lũ tràn qua; \q vực sâu cất tiếng; \q nó giơ tay lên cao.
vi.B: Các núi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và quằn quại; \q một cơn lũ nước cuồn cuộn tràn qua; \q vực sâu gầm thét \q và giơ tay lên cao.
vi.R: Khi các núi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, chúng rung chuyển. \q Nước lũ ào ạt chảy qua. \q Đại dương sâu thẳm gầm vang \q và dâng sóng lên cao.

ko.L: 산들이 주님을 보고 몸부림쳤습니다. \q 거센 물이 휩쓸고 지나갔습니다. \q 깊은 물이 소리를 내고, \q 높이 그 손을 들었습니다.
ko.B: 산들이 주님을 보고 몸부림쳤고, \q 거센 물줄기가 휩쓸고 지나갔습니다. \q 깊은 바다가 크게 울부짖으며 \q 그 손을 높이 들었습니다.
ko.R: 산들이 주님을 보고 흔들렸습니다. \q 큰물이 세차게 흘러갔습니다. \q 깊은 바다가 소리를 지르며 \q 물결을 높이 쳐들었습니다.

decisions.choice: the mountains saw you and writhed ... the deep gave its voice: Psalm 77:17-19
decisions.reason: Psalm 77:17-19 says: "The waters saw you, God; ... the deeps trembled", with storm and thunder, in a psalm that also recalls the exodus. Habakkuk applies the picture to the mountains and the deep.

decisions.choice: it lifted its hands on high: the deep raised its waves
decisions.reason: The deep is pictured as a living thing that cries out and lifts its hands, perhaps in fear or surrender. The picture is of its waves rising high.

decisions.choice: raised its waves high
decisions.reason: Readable says what the deep's "hands" are (m2).

decisions.choice: "te vieron ... se retorcieron"
decisions.reason: The verse echoes Psalm 77:17; the Spanish uses that psalm's words ("te vieron", "se retorcieron") where the Hebrew agrees.
