records.literal_gloss: Sun, moon stood still [in their] dwelling; at [the] light of your arrows they went, at [the] brightness of [the] lightning of your spear.

en.L: Sun [and] moon stood still in [their] dwelling \q at the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows [as] they flew, \q at the gleam of the lightning of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} spear.
en.B: Sun and moon stood still in the heavens \q at the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} flying arrows, \q at the flash of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} gleaming spear.
en.R: The sun and moon stopped in the sky \q when they saw {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows flash by \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} spear shine like lightning.

es.L: [El] sol [y la] luna se detuvieron en [su] morada \q a la luz de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} saetas [que] volaban, \q al resplandor del relámpago de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lanza.
es.B: El sol y la luna se detuvieron en el cielo \q a la luz de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} flechas que volaban, \q al brillo de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lanza reluciente.
es.R: El sol y la luna se detuvieron en el cielo \q cuando vieron pasar {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} flechas como relámpagos \q y brillar {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lanza como un rayo.

fr.L: Soleil [et] lune se sont arrêtés dans [leur] demeure \q à la lumière de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches [qui] filaient, \q à l’éclat de l’éclair de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lance.
fr.B: Le soleil et la lune se sont arrêtés dans le ciel \q à la lumière de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches qui volaient, \q à l’éclat de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lance étincelante.
fr.R: Le soleil et la lune se sont arrêtés dans le ciel \q quand ils ont vu {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches filer comme l’éclair \q et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lance briller comme la foudre.

sw.L: Jua [na] mwezi vilisimama tuli katika makao [yao] \q kwa nuru ya mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} [ilipo]ruka, \q kwa mng'ao wa umeme wa mkuki {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Jua na mwezi vilisimama tuli angani \q kwa nuru ya mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} inayoruka, \q kwa mmeto wa mkuki {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ung'aao.
sw.R: Jua na mwezi vilisimama angani \q vilipoona mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ikipita kwa kasi \q na mkuki {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ukimetameta kama umeme.

vi.L: Mặt trời [và] mặt trăng đứng yên trong chỗ ở [của chúng] \q trước ánh sáng của các mũi tên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [khi] chúng bay đi, \q trước tia chớp lóe sáng của ngọn giáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Mặt trời và mặt trăng đứng yên trên trời \q trước ánh sáng của những mũi tên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang bay, \q trước ánh chớp của ngọn giáo sáng ngời của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Mặt trời và mặt trăng dừng lại trên bầu trời \q khi thấy mũi tên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lóe sáng bay qua \q và ngọn giáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chói lòa như tia chớp.

ko.L: 해와 달이 [그] 처소에 멈추어 섰습니다. \q 주님의 화살들이 날아가는 빛 때문에, \q 주님의 창의 번쩍이는 번개 때문에 [그렇게 되었습니다].
ko.B: 해와 달이 하늘에 멈추어 섰습니다. \q 주님의 화살이 빛을 내며 날아가고, \q 주님의 창이 번개처럼 번쩍였기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 해와 달이 하늘에서 멈추었습니다. \q 주님의 화살이 번쩍이며 날아가고 \q 주님의 창이 번개처럼 빛나는 것을 보았기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: sun and moon stood still: the battle of Gibeon
decisions.reason: When Joshua fought at Gibeon, "the sun stood still, and the moon stopped" until Israel had won (Joshua 10:12-13). Habakkuk recalls it among the LORD's acts for his people. "Dwelling" is their lofty home in the sky.

decisions.choice: your arrows ... your spear: lightning
decisions.reason: God's arrows and spear are the lightning of the storm (Psalm 18:15; 77:18-19). Their light outshines the sun and moon.

decisions.choice: in the sky (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "in the sky" for "in their dwelling" (m1).

records.literal_gloss: In indignation you march through [the] earth; in anger you thresh nations.

en.L: In indignation {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} marched through [the] earth; \q in anger {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} threshed [the] nations.
en.B: In fury {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} strode across the earth; \q in anger {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} trampled the nations.
en.R: You were angry as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} marched across the earth. \q In {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} crushed the nations like grain.

es.L: Con indignación marchaste por [la] tierra; \q con ira trillaste [a las] naciones.
es.B: Con furor recorriste la tierra; \q con ira pisoteaste a las naciones.
es.R: Estabas enojado mientras marchabas por la tierra. \q En {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enojo aplastaste a las naciones como se trilla el grano.

fr.L: Avec indignation {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as parcouru la terre ; \q avec colère {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as battu les nations.
fr.B: Dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} fureur {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as traversé la terre à grands pas ; \q dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as piétiné les nations.
fr.R: Tu étais en colère quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as traversé la terre. \q Dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as écrasé les nations comme on écrase le grain.

sw.L: Kwa ghadhabu ulipita katika nchi; \q kwa hasira uliyapura mataifa.
sw.B: Kwa ghadhabu ulipita katika dunia; \q kwa hasira uliyakanyaga mataifa.
sw.R: Ulikuwa na hasira ulipopita katika dunia. \q Kwa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} uliyaponda mataifa kama nafaka inavyopurwa.

vi.L: Trong cơn phẫn nộ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đi khắp đất; \q trong cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đạp các nước như đạp lúa.
vi.B: Trong cơn thịnh nộ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sải bước khắp đất; \q trong cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giày đạp các nước.
vi.R: Ngài nổi giận khi đi khắp mặt đất. \q Trong cơn giận, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghiền nát các nước như người ta đập lúa.

ko.L: 주님께서 진노하시며 땅을 행진하셨고, \q 분노하시며 민족들을 타작하셨습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 노하셔서 땅을 가로질러 나아가셨고, \q 분노하셔서 민족들을 짓밟으셨습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서는 화가 나셔서 온 땅을 가로질러 걸어가셨습니다. \q 화가 나셔서 곡식을 짓밟듯이 민족들을 짓밟으셨습니다.

decisions.choice: you threshed the nations
decisions.reason: Threshing was done by animals treading the grain or by a heavy sledge dragged over it. It is a picture of crushing defeat (Micah 4:13; Isaiah 41:15; Amos 1:3).

decisions.choice: trampled (B); crushed ... like grain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "trampled"; Readable keeps the threshing picture by saying "like grain".

source.text: יָצָ֨אתָ֙ לְיֵ֣שַׁע עַמֶּ֔ךָ לְיֵ֖שַׁע אֶת־מְשִׁיחֶ֑ךָ מָחַ֤צְתָּ רֹּאשׁ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית רָשָׁ֔ע עָר֛וֹת יְס֥וֹד עַד־צַוָּ֖אר סֶֽלָה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: You went out for [the] salvation of your people, for [the] salvation of your anointed; you crushed [the] head from [the] house of [the] wicked, laying bare [the] foundation to [the] neck. Selah.

en.L: You went forth for [the] salvation of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q for saving {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} smashed [the] head from [the] house of [the] wicked, \q laying [it] bare from foundation to neck. Selah
en.B: You went out to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed one. \q You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, \q stripping it bare from the foundation up to the neck. Selah
en.R: You came out to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, \q to save {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chosen king. \q You crushed the leader of the wicked nation \q and destroyed his house completely, from top to bottom. Selah

es.L: Saliste para [la] salvación de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, \q para salvar a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ungido; \q aplastaste [la] cabeza de [la] casa del impío, \q desnudándo[la] desde el cimiento hasta el cuello. Selah
es.B: Saliste para salvar a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, \q para salvar a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ungido. \q Aplastaste la cabeza de la casa del malvado, \q dejándola al desnudo desde el cimiento hasta el cuello. Selah
es.R: Saliste para salvar a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, \q para salvar al rey que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} escogiste. \q Aplastaste al jefe de la nación malvada \q y destruiste su casa por completo, de arriba abajo. Selah

fr.L: Tu es sorti pour le salut de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, \q pour sauver {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} oint ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fracassé la tête de la maison du méchant, \q [la] mettant à nu du fondement jusqu’au cou. Sélah
fr.B: Tu es sorti pour sauver {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, \q pour sauver celui que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as oint. \q Tu as écrasé la tête de la maison du méchant, \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as mise à nu des fondations jusqu’au cou. Sélah
fr.R: Tu es venu sauver {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, \q sauver le roi que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as choisi. \q Tu as écrasé le chef de la nation méchante \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as détruit sa maison complètement, de fond en comble. Sélah

sw.L: Ulitoka kwa ajili ya wokovu wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q kwa ajili ya kumwokoa mpakwa mafuta {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}; \q uliponda kichwa cha nyumba ya mwovu, \q ukiifunua kutoka msingi hadi shingo. Sela
sw.B: Ulitoka kuwaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q kumwokoa mpakwa mafuta {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}. \q Uliponda kichwa cha nyumba ya mwovu, \q ukiiacha tupu kutoka msingi hadi shingo. Sela
sw.R: Ulitoka kuwaokoa watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q kumwokoa mfalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} uliyemchagua. \q Ulimponda kiongozi wa taifa ovu \q na kuiangamiza nyumba yake kabisa, kutoka juu hadi chini. Sela

vi.L: Ngài đã ra đi để cứu rỗi dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q để cứu người được xức dầu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đập nát đầu của nhà kẻ ác, \q lột trần [nó] từ nền móng cho đến cổ. Sê-la
vi.B: Ngài đã ra đi để cứu dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q để cứu người được xức dầu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Ngài đã đập nát đầu của nhà kẻ ác, \q lột trần nó từ nền cho đến tận cổ. Sê-la
vi.R: Ngài đã đến để cứu dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q để cứu vị vua {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chọn. \q Ngài đã đánh tan kẻ cầm đầu của dân gian ác \q và phá hủy hoàn toàn nhà hắn, từ trên xuống dưới. Sê-la

ko.L: 주님께서 주님의 백성의 구원을 위하여, \q 주님의 기름 부음 받은 자를 구원하시려고 나오셨습니다. \q 악인의 집에서 머리를 부수시고, \q 기초부터 목까지 드러내셨습니다. 셀라
ko.B: 주님께서 주님의 백성을 구원하시려고, \q 주님께서 기름 부으신 이를 구원하시려고 나오셨습니다. \q 주님께서 악인의 집의 머리를 부수시고, \q 기초에서 목까지 벗겨 내셨습니다. 셀라
ko.R: 주님께서 주님의 백성을 구하시려고 나오셨습니다. \q 주님께서 택하신 왕을 구하시려고 나오셨습니다. \q 주님께서 악한 나라의 우두머리를 부수시고 \q 그 집을 위에서 아래까지 완전히 무너뜨리셨습니다. 셀라

decisions.choice: your anointed: the king
decisions.reason: The anointed one is the king of God's people, anointed with oil when he was made king (1 Samuel 16:13; Psalm 2:2; 18:51). In this line it stands in parallel with "your people", so the king may stand for the people as a whole (Psalm 28:8). The poem does not name a particular king.

decisions.choice: crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck: total defeat
decisions.reason: Two pictures are joined: a house demolished down to its foundations, and an enemy struck on the head and stripped. The "head" is the leader of the wicked nation; the line says that he and his house are destroyed completely. The details of the line are uncertain.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in this chapter (verses 3, 9 and 13). It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude. It is not part of what is said.

decisions.choice: anointed (L, B); chosen king (R)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 45:1, Readable says "chosen" for "anointed", and adds "king" (m1). The anointed one takes no deity_pronoun span. Selah stays at the end of the verse, as the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: the leader of the wicked nation ... from top to bottom
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two pictures mean (m2).

decisions.choice: "tu ungido" (L, B); "el rey que tú escogiste" (R)
decisions.reason: The anointed one is the king; L and B keep "ungido", lowercase and with no deity_pronoun span, and R says who is meant.

decisions.choice: "ton oint" (L), "celui que tu as oint" (B), "le roi que tu as choisi" (R); the anointed one takes no deity_pronoun span, only God's "ton" / "tu" do
decisions.reason: As Isaiah 45:1 R and the English (m1).

decisions.choice: "mpakwa mafuta wako" (L, B); "mfalme wako uliyemchagua" (R)
decisions.reason: The anointed one is the king of Israel, as the meaning decision says; "mpakwa mafuta" is lowercase and takes no christos span, as Daniel 9:25 in the term sheet. The free possessive "wako" refers to God and so takes the span.

decisions.choice: "người được xức dầu của Ngài" (L, B) / "vị vua Ngài đã chọn" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the anointed is the king; lowercase and with no deity span, as the terms note gives for the LORD's anointed.

decisions.choice: "your anointed" is "주님의 기름 부음 받은 자" (L), "주님께서 기름 부으신 이" (B), "주님께서 택하신 왕" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the anointed is the king of God's people, as the meaning decision says; no christos span, since the English has none.

source.text: נָקַ֤בְתָּ בְמַטָּיו֙ רֹ֣אשׁ פְּרָזָ֔יו יִסְעֲר֖וּ לַהֲפִיצֵ֑נִי עֲלִ֣יצֻתָ֔ם כְּמוֹ־לֶאֱכֹ֥ל עָנִ֖י בַּמִּסְתָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: You pierced with his shafts [the] head of his warriors; they storm to scatter me; their exultation [was] as to devour [the] afflicted in secret.

en.L: You pierced with his own shafts the head of his warriors \q [when] they stormed out to scatter me, \q their exulting [was] as [if] to devour \q the afflicted in [a] hiding place.
en.B: With his own arrows {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pierced the head of his warriors \q when they stormed out to scatter me, \q gloating as if about to devour \q the helpless in their hiding place.
en.R: You used the enemy's own weapons to kill the leader of his soldiers \q when they rushed out like a storm to scatter me. \q They were happy, like someone about to attack \q a poor person who is hiding.

es.L: Traspasaste con sus propias lanzas la cabeza de sus guerreros \q [cuando] irrumpieron para dispersarme; \q su regocijo [era] como [para] devorar \q al afligido en [un] escondite.
es.B: Con sus propias flechas traspasaste la cabeza de sus guerreros \q cuando irrumpieron como tormenta para dispersarme, \q regodeándose como quien va a devorar \q al indefenso en su escondite.
es.R: Usaste las propias armas del enemigo para matar al jefe de sus soldados \q cuando se lanzaron como una tormenta para dispersarme. \q Estaban felices, como alguien que está a punto de atacar \q a un pobre que se esconde.

fr.L: Tu as percé avec ses propres traits la tête de ses guerriers \q [quand] ils se sont rués pour me disperser ; \q leur exultation [était] comme [pour] dévorer \q le malheureux dans [une] cachette.
fr.B: Avec ses propres flèches {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as percé la tête de ses guerriers \q quand ils déferlaient pour me disperser, \q jubilant comme s’ils allaient dévorer \q le pauvre dans sa cachette.
fr.R: Tu as pris les armes de l’ennemi pour tuer le chef de ses soldats \q quand ils se sont précipités comme une tempête pour me disperser. \q Ils étaient joyeux, comme quelqu’un qui va attaquer \q un pauvre qui se cache.

sw.L: Ulikichoma kwa mishale yake mwenyewe kichwa cha mashujaa wake \q [walipo]kuja kama dhoruba kunitawanya, \q furaha yao [ilikuwa] kama [ya] kumla \q mnyonge mahali pa kujificha.
sw.B: Kwa mishale yake mwenyewe ulikichoma kichwa cha mashujaa wake \q walipokuja kama dhoruba kunitawanya, \q wakishangilia kana kwamba wanakaribia kumla \q mnyonge aliyejificha.
sw.R: Ulitumia silaha za adui mwenyewe kumuua kiongozi wa askari wake \q walipokuja kama dhoruba kunitawanya. \q Walifurahi kama mtu anayekaribia kumshambulia \q maskini aliyejificha.

vi.L: Ngài đã dùng chính các mũi giáo của nó đâm thủng đầu các chiến binh nó \q [khi] chúng xông tới như bão để làm tôi tan lạc; \q sự hớn hở của chúng [như thể] sắp nuốt \q người khốn khổ trong nơi ẩn náu.
vi.B: Ngài dùng chính các mũi tên của nó mà đâm thủng đầu các chiến binh nó, \q khi chúng ào tới như bão để đánh tan tôi, \q hả hê như sắp nuốt chửng \q kẻ cô thế trong nơi ẩn nấp.
vi.R: Ngài đã dùng chính vũ khí của kẻ thù để giết tên chỉ huy quân lính của nó, \q khi chúng ào tới như cơn bão để đánh tan tôi. \q Chúng hớn hở như kẻ sắp tấn công \q một người nghèo đang trốn tránh.

ko.L: 주님께서 그의 [창]대로 그의 용사들의 머리를 찌르셨습니다. \q 그들이 저를 흩으려고 폭풍처럼 몰려왔을 [때], \q 그들의 기뻐함은 \q 은밀한 곳에서 가난한 자를 삼키려는 것 같았습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 그의 화살로 그의 용사들의 머리를 꿰뚫으셨습니다. \q 그들이 저를 흩으려고 폭풍처럼 몰려올 때에, \q 숨어 있는 가난한 사람을 \q 삼키려는 듯이 기뻐 날뛰던 자들입니다.
ko.R: 주님께서는 원수의 무기로 그 군대의 우두머리를 죽이셨습니다. \q 그들이 저희를 흩어 버리려고 폭풍처럼 달려들 때였습니다. \q 그들은 숨어 있는 가난한 사람을 \q 덮치려는 사람처럼 기뻐했습니다.

decisions.choice: with his own shafts the head of his warriors: an obscure line
alternatives: with your arrows you pierced the head of his leaders
decisions.reason: The word for "shafts" is the one translated "arrows" in verse 9; it can also mean staffs. The word for "warriors" is rare and uncertain: it may mean warriors, leaders or villagers. The line seems to say that God turned the enemy's own weapons against him, as when enemies destroyed one another (Judges 7:22; 1 Samuel 14:20). The written text and the reading in the margin differ slightly in one word without changing the sense.

decisions.choice: to scatter me: the prophet speaks for his people
decisions.reason: Habakkuk says "me", speaking as one of the people whom the enemy came to scatter.

decisions.choice: as if to devour the afflicted in a hiding place
decisions.reason: The enemy is pictured as a robber or a lion lying in wait to seize the helpless (Psalm 10:8-9; 17:12).

decisions.choice: the enemy's own weapons; the leader of his soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the line seems to mean (m1).

decisions.choice: "con" for the prophet's "me" while he speaks to God (8-15)
decisions.reason: He speaks for his people (m2) in a prayer addressed to God, so he says "con"; "tôi" returns in verse 16, where he speaks of himself.

source.text: דָּרַ֥כְתָּ בַיָּ֖ם סוּסֶ֑יךָ חֹ֖מֶר מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: You trod on the sea [with] your horses, [the] heap of waters many.

en.L: You trod on the sea with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q the heaping of many waters.
en.B: You trampled the sea with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses, \q churning the mighty waters.
en.R: You rode {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} horses across the sea, \q stirring up the great waters.

es.L: Pisaste el mar con {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caballos, \q el oleaje de muchas aguas.
es.B: Pisoteaste el mar con {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caballos, \q agitando las aguas poderosas.
es.R: Cabalgaste con {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} caballos sobre el mar \q y agitaste las grandes aguas.

fr.L: Tu as foulé la mer avec {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chevaux, \q le bouillonnement des grandes eaux.
fr.B: Tu as foulé la mer avec {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chevaux, \q faisant bouillonner les eaux puissantes.
fr.R: Tu as traversé la mer avec {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chevaux, \q en soulevant les grandes eaux.

sw.L: Uliikanyaga bahari kwa farasi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q mrundiko wa maji mengi.
sw.B: Uliikanyaga bahari kwa farasi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q ukiyavuruga maji makuu.
sw.R: Uliwaendesha farasi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kupita katika bahari, \q ukiyachafua maji makuu.

vi.L: Ngài đã giẫm trên biển bằng các ngựa của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q trên những ngọn nước lớn dồn đống.
vi.B: Ngài đã giày đạp biển bằng các ngựa của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q khuấy động những dòng nước lớn.
vi.R: Ngài cưỡi ngựa băng qua biển, \q khuấy động những dòng nước lớn.

ko.L: 주님께서 주님의 말들로 바다를, \q 많은 물의 더미를 밟으셨습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 말을 타고 바다를 짓밟으시니 \q 큰물이 소용돌이쳤습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 말을 타고 바다를 건너가시니 \q 큰물이 출렁거렸습니다.

decisions.choice: you trod on the sea: the crossing of the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The poem returns to the sea of verse 8. At the exodus "the waters were heaped up" (Exodus 15:8), and "your way was through the sea, your path through the great waters" (Psalm 77:20). The word for "heaping" may also mean the foaming or surging of the water.

decisions.choice: churning (B); stirring up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the heaped, surging water as churned or stirred up by the horses.

source.text: שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי׀וַתִּרְגַּ֣ז בִּטְנִ֗י לְקוֹל֙ צָלֲל֣וּ שְׂפָתַ֔י יָב֥וֹא רָקָ֛ב בַּעֲצָמַ֖י וְתַחְתַּ֣י אֶרְגָּ֑ז אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָנ֨וּחַ֙ לְי֣וֹם צָרָ֔ה לַעֲל֖וֹת לְעַ֥ם יְגוּדֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I heard, and my belly trembled; at [the] sound my lips quivered; rottenness entered into my bones, and under me I trembled, [so] that I will wait quietly for [the] day of distress, to come up on [the] people [who] invade us.

en.L: I heard, and my belly trembled; at the sound my lips quivered; \q rottenness entered my bones, and where I stood I trembled; \q yet I will wait quietly for [the] day of distress \q to come up on [the] people [who] invade us.
en.B: I heard, and my body trembled; my lips quivered at the sound. \q Decay entered my bones, and my legs shook beneath me. \q Yet I will wait quietly for the day of trouble \q to come on the people who invade us.
en.R: When I heard this, my whole body shook. My lips trembled with fear. \q My bones felt weak, and my legs shook under me. \q But I will wait calmly for the day of disaster \q that will come on the nation that attacks us.

es.L: Oí, y se estremecieron mis entrañas; al sonido temblaron mis labios; \q entró podredumbre en mis huesos, y donde estaba temblé; \q aun así esperaré tranquilo [el] día de la angustia \q que vendrá sobre [el] pueblo [que] nos invade.
es.B: Lo oí, y todo mi cuerpo tembló; mis labios temblaron al oír el sonido. \q La debilidad entró en mis huesos, y mis piernas temblaron debajo de mí. \q Aun así, esperaré tranquilo el día de la angustia \q que vendrá sobre el pueblo que nos invade.
es.R: Cuando oí esto, todo mi cuerpo se estremeció. Mis labios temblaron de miedo. \q Sentí débiles los huesos, y me temblaban las piernas. \q Pero esperaré con calma el día del desastre \q que vendrá sobre la nación que nos ataca.

fr.L: J’ai entendu, et mes entrailles ont tremblé ; à ce bruit mes lèvres ont frémi ; \q la pourriture est entrée dans mes os, et là où je me tenais j’ai tremblé ; \q pourtant j’attendrai en silence le jour de la détresse \q [qui] montera contre le peuple [qui] nous envahit.
fr.B: J’ai entendu, et tout mon corps a tremblé ; à ce bruit mes lèvres ont frémi. \q La pourriture a pénétré mes os, et mes jambes ont tremblé sous moi. \q Pourtant j’attendrai calmement le jour de la détresse \q qui viendra sur le peuple qui nous envahit.
fr.R: Quand j’ai entendu cela, tout mon corps a tremblé. Mes lèvres ont tremblé de peur. \q J’ai senti mes os faiblir, et mes jambes tremblaient sous moi. \q Mais j’attendrai calmement le jour du malheur \q qui viendra sur la nation qui nous attaque.

sw.L: Nilisikia, na tumbo langu likatetemeka; kwa sauti hiyo midomo yangu ilitetemeka; \q uozo uliingia mifupani mwangu, na mahali niliposimama nilitetemeka; \q lakini nitangoja kwa utulivu siku ya taabu \q iwajie watu [wanaotu]shambulia.
sw.B: Nilisikia, na mwili wangu ukatetemeka; midomo yangu ilitetemeka kwa sauti hiyo. \q Uozo uliingia mifupani mwangu, na miguu yangu ikatetemeka chini yangu. \q Lakini nitangoja kwa utulivu siku ya taabu \q iwajie watu wanaotushambulia.
sw.R: Niliposikia haya, mwili wangu wote ulitetemeka. Midomo yangu ilitetemeka kwa hofu. \q Mifupa yangu ilidhoofika, na miguu yangu ikatetemeka chini yangu. \q Lakini nitangoja kwa utulivu siku ya maafa \q itakayolijia taifa linalotushambulia.

vi.L: Tôi nghe, và bụng tôi run rẩy; nghe tiếng ấy môi tôi run run; \q sự mục nát vào trong xương cốt tôi, và tại chỗ tôi đứng, tôi run rẩy; \q nhưng tôi sẽ yên lặng chờ ngày hoạn nạn \q đến trên dân [đang] xâm lăng chúng tôi.
vi.B: Tôi nghe, và toàn thân tôi run rẩy; môi tôi run lên khi nghe tiếng ấy. \q Xương cốt tôi như mục rữa, và đôi chân tôi run lẩy bẩy. \q Nhưng tôi sẽ lặng lẽ chờ ngày hoạn nạn \q giáng trên dân đang xâm lăng chúng tôi.
vi.R: Khi nghe điều này, toàn thân tôi run rẩy. Môi tôi run lên vì sợ. \q Xương cốt tôi rã rời, và chân tôi run lẩy bẩy. \q Nhưng tôi sẽ bình tĩnh chờ đợi ngày tai họa \q sẽ giáng xuống trên dân tộc đang tấn công chúng tôi.

ko.L: 내가 들었을 때, 내 배가 떨리고, 그 소리에 내 입술이 떨렸다. \q 썩음이 내 뼈 속에 들어오고, 내가 선 자리에서 떨었다. \q 그러나 나는 우리를 침략하는 백성에게 \q 재난의 날이 닥치기를 조용히 기다리겠다.
ko.B: 나는 듣고 온몸이 떨렸고, 그 소리에 입술이 떨렸다. \q 뼈가 썩어 들어가는 듯하고, 다리가 후들거렸다. \q 그러나 나는 우리를 침략한 백성에게 \q 환난의 날이 닥치기를 잠잠히 기다리겠다.
ko.R: 이 말을 듣자 나는 온몸이 떨렸다. 두려워서 입술이 떨렸다. \q 뼈마디에 힘이 빠지고 다리가 후들후들 떨렸다. \q 그러나 나는 우리를 공격하는 나라에 \q 재앙의 날이 닥치기를 조용히 기다리겠다.

decisions.choice: belly, lips, bones: terror felt through the whole body
decisions.reason: Habakkuk describes overwhelming fear in bodily terms, as Jeremiah 23:9 and Daniel 10:8 do. The "belly" is the inner body; "rottenness in the bones" means that strength has drained away (Proverbs 12:4; 14:30).

decisions.choice: yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress
alternatives: I tremble because I must wait for the day of distress
decisions.reason: The word that joins the lines can mean "yet", "so that" or "because". It is taken here to mean that, though he trembles, he will wait calmly for the day when distress comes on the invader, as the vision promised (2:3). It may also mean that he trembles because he must wait through the day of distress coming on his own people.

decisions.choice: my body (B, R); my legs shook beneath me (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "body" for "belly" and turn "under me I trembled" into the plain sense: his legs gave way.

decisions.choice: "tôi" and "chúng tôi" from verse 16 on
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks of himself and his people, no longer to God.

decisions.choice: From 3:16 to the end Habakkuk speaks in the plain style with "나", and of God with -시- (3:18–19)
decisions.reason: The prophet turns from addressing God to telling his own response, so the speech level turns with him, as in the psalms.

source.text: כִּֽי־תְאֵנָ֣ה לֹֽא־תִפְרָ֗ח וְאֵ֤ין יְבוּל֙ בַּגְּפָנִ֔ים כִּחֵשׁ֙ מַעֲשֵׂה־זַ֔יִת וּשְׁדֵמ֖וֹת לֹא־עָ֣שָׂה אֹ֑כֶל גָּזַ֤ר מִמִּכְלָה֙ צֹ֔אן וְאֵ֥ין בָּקָ֖ר בָּרְפָתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] fig tree not does blossom, and there is no produce on the vines; fails [the] yield of [the] olive, and fields not do produce food; is cut off from [the] fold [the] flock, and there are no cattle in the stalls,

en.L: Though [the] fig tree does not blossom and there is no fruit on the vines, \q [though the] yield of [the] olive fails \q and [the] fields do not make food, \q [though the] flock is cut off from [the] fold \q and there are no cattle in the stalls,
en.B: Though the fig tree does not flower and the vines bear no grapes, \q though the olive harvest fails \q and the fields yield nothing to eat, \q though the sheep vanish from the pen \q and the stalls hold no cattle,
en.R: The fig trees may not bloom, and there may be no grapes on the vines. \q The olive trees may give no olives, \q and the fields may produce no food. \q There may be no sheep in the pens \q and no cattle in the barns.

es.L: Aunque [la] higuera no florezca y no haya fruto en las vides, \q [aunque] falle [el] producto del olivo \q y [los] campos no den alimento, \q [aunque] desaparezca [el] rebaño del redil \q y no haya ganado en los establos,
es.B: Aunque la higuera no dé flores y las vides no den uvas, \q aunque falle la cosecha del olivo \q y los campos no produzcan nada que comer, \q aunque se acaben las ovejas del redil \q y no haya vacas en los establos,
es.R: Puede ser que las higueras no florezcan y que no haya uvas en las vides. \q Puede ser que los olivos no den aceitunas \q y que los campos no produzcan alimentos. \q Puede ser que no haya ovejas en los corrales \q ni vacas en los establos.

fr.L: Même si le figuier ne bourgeonne pas et qu’il n’y a pas de fruit aux vignes, \q [même si] le rapport de l’olivier fait défaut \q et que les champs ne donnent pas de nourriture, \q [même si] le petit bétail est retranché de l’enclos \q et qu’il n’y a pas de bœufs dans les étables,
fr.B: Même si le figuier ne fleurit plus et que les vignes ne portent pas de raisin, \q même si la récolte des olives fait défaut \q et que les champs ne donnent rien à manger, \q même si les moutons disparaissent de l’enclos \q et qu’il n’y a plus de bétail dans les étables,
fr.R: Il se peut que les figuiers ne fleurissent pas et qu’il n’y ait pas de raisin sur les vignes. \q Il se peut que les oliviers ne donnent pas d’olives \q et que les champs ne produisent aucune nourriture. \q Il se peut qu’il n’y ait plus de moutons dans les enclos \q ni de vaches dans les étables.

sw.L: Ingawa mtini hauchanui, wala hakuna matunda katika mizabibu, \q [ingawa] mazao ya mzeituni yanakoma \q na mashamba hayatoi chakula, \q [ingawa] kundi limekatiliwa mbali na zizi \q wala hakuna ng'ombe katika mazizi,
sw.B: Ingawa mtini hautoi maua, na mizabibu haizai zabibu, \q ingawa mavuno ya zeituni yanakosekana \q na mashamba hayatoi chochote cha kula, \q ingawa kondoo wanatoweka zizini \q na mabanda hayana ng'ombe,
sw.R: Huenda mitini isichanue maua, na huenda kusiwe na zabibu katika mizabibu. \q Huenda mizeituni isizae zeituni, \q na huenda mashamba yasitoe chakula. \q Huenda kusiwe na kondoo katika mazizi \q wala ng'ombe katika mabanda.

vi.L: Dù cây vả không trổ hoa và không có trái trên các cây nho, \q [dù] hoa lợi của cây ô-liu thất bại \q và đồng ruộng không sinh ra thức ăn, \q [dù] bầy chiên bị dứt khỏi chuồng \q và không có bò trong chuồng,
vi.B: Dù cây vả không trổ hoa, và cây nho không ra trái, \q dù mùa ô-liu thất bát \q và đồng ruộng chẳng sinh ra gì để ăn, \q dù chiên biến mất khỏi ràn \q và chuồng không còn con bò nào,
vi.R: Cây vả có thể không ra hoa, cây nho có thể không có trái. \q Cây ô-liu có thể không cho trái, \q và đồng ruộng có thể không sinh ra lương thực. \q Có thể không còn con chiên nào trong ràn \q và không còn con bò nào trong chuồng.

ko.L: 비록 무화과나무에 꽃이 피지 않고 포도나무에 열매가 없으며, \q 올리브나무의 소출이 끊어지고 \q 밭들이 먹을 것을 내지 못하며, \q 우리에서 양 떼가 끊어지고 \q 외양간에 소가 없을지라도,
ko.B: 무화과나무에 꽃이 피지 않고 포도나무에 포도가 열리지 않아도, \q 올리브 수확이 없고 \q 밭에서 먹을 것이 나지 않아도, \q 우리에 양이 하나도 없고 \q 외양간에 소가 없어도,
ko.R: 무화과나무에 꽃이 피지 않을 수도 있다. 포도나무에 포도가 하나도 없을 수도 있다. \q 올리브나무에 올리브가 열리지 않을 수도 있다. \q 밭에서 먹을 것이 하나도 나지 않을 수도 있다. \q 우리에 양이 한 마리도 없을 수도 있다. \q 외양간에 소가 한 마리도 없을 수도 있다.

decisions.choice: though: even if everything fails
decisions.reason: The verse lists everything a farming people lived on: figs, grapes, olives, grain, sheep and cattle (Deuteronomy 8:8; Joel 1:10-12). The word at the start may mean "though" or "for": either the prophet imagines the worst, or he describes the ruin the invasion will bring. Either way, verse 18 says that his joy does not depend on them.

decisions.choice: the flock is cut off from the fold
decisions.reason: The sheep and goats are gone from their pen, taken by the enemy or dead from want of pasture.

decisions.choice: Though (L, B); may (R); the comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 18, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma. Readable makes each line a sentence with "may" and begins verse 18 with "Even then".

decisions.choice: "Aunque" (L, B); "Puede ser que" (R)
decisions.reason: L and B keep the one long sentence that runs into verse 18, ending with a comma, as the English does; R makes short sentences.

decisions.choice: "Même si … " (L, B), with the sentence running on into verse 18; "Il se peut que …" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *ki* here is concessive, as the English "Though". French says it with "Même si" and keeps the long sentence across the verse break at L and B, which also keeps the wording away from the familiar French versions of 3:17-19.

decisions.choice: "Ingawa …" (L), "Hata kama …" (B), ending with a comma; "Huenda …" (R)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 18, as the English; drafted from the gloss, away from the Union Version's wording.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 18, ending each verse with a comma at L and B
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "though ... yet I" spans verses 17-18; the English keeps the comma, and Literal and Balanced do the same; Readable closes the verse as its own sentence.

decisions.choice: "Though" is "비록 … 없을지라도" (L) and "… 없어도" (B), ending in a comma that runs into 3:18; Readable says "…할 수도 있다"
decisions.reason: Drafted from the gloss and away from the familiar older lines of 3:17–18; Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's one long sentence across the two verses, as the English does, and Readable makes each line its own sentence.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֖י בַּיהוָ֣ה אֶעְל֑וֹזָה אָגִ֖ילָה בֵּאלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׁעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: yet I, in Yahweh I will exult; I will rejoice in [the] God of my salvation.

en.L: yet I, in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I will exult; \q I will rejoice in [the] God of my salvation.
en.B: yet I will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q I will find joy in God, my Savior.
en.R: Even then I will be glad because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will be joyful because God saves me.

es.L: pero yo en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me regocijaré; \q me alegraré en [el] Dios de mi salvación.
es.B: aun así yo me alegraré en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; \q me gozaré en Dios, mi Salvador.
es.R: Aun así, yo estaré feliz por lo que es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Me llenaré de alegría porque Dios me salva.

fr.L: moi, malgré tout, dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} j’exulterai ; \q je jubilerai dans le Dieu de mon salut.
fr.B: moi, pourtant, je me réjouirai dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; \q je trouverai ma joie en Dieu, mon Sauveur.
fr.R: Même alors, je serai heureux grâce {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. \q Je serai plein de joie, parce que Dieu me sauve.

sw.L: lakini mimi, katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} nitashangilia; \q nitafurahi katika Mungu wa wokovu wangu.
sw.B: lakini mimi nitafurahi katika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q nitamfurahia Mungu, Mwokozi wangu.
sw.R: Hata hivyo nitafurahi kwa sababu ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Nitajaa furaha kwa sababu Mungu ananiokoa.

vi.L: thì tôi, trong {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tôi sẽ hớn hở; \q tôi sẽ vui mừng trong Đức Chúa Trời của sự cứu rỗi tôi.
vi.B: thì tôi vẫn vui mừng trong {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q tôi sẽ hân hoan trong Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng Cứu Rỗi tôi.
vi.R: Dù vậy, tôi vẫn vui mừng vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Tôi sẽ hân hoan vì Đức Chúa Trời cứu tôi.

ko.L: 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 안에서 기뻐 뛰고, \q 나의 구원의 하나님 안에서 즐거워하겠다.
ko.B: 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 때문에 기뻐하고, \q 나를 구원하시는 하나님 때문에 즐거워하겠다.
ko.R: 그때에도 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 때문에 기뻐하겠다. \q 하나님께서 나를 구해 주시니 즐거워하겠다.

decisions.choice: yet I will exult in the LORD: joy in God himself
decisions.reason: The prophet who began with complaint ends with joy. His joy rests not on the harvest or on his circumstances but on the LORD himself, the God who saves him (Psalm 73:25-26). "I" is emphatic in the Hebrew: whatever happens, I will rejoice.

decisions.choice: the God of my salvation: God who rescues me
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in verses 8 and 13 for the LORD's rescue of his people. The phrase is common in the Psalms (Psalm 18:47; 25:5).

decisions.choice: God, my Savior (B); because God saves me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "Savior" and "saves" for "salvation", the noun's sense here (m2).

decisions.choice: "yo, sin embargo, en el SEÑOR exultaré" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the emphatic "I" and the Hebrew order (m1), worded away from the familiar versions.

decisions.choice: "moi, pourtant, dans le SEIGNEUR je bondirai de joie" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the emphatic "I" and the Hebrew order (m1); the line is drafted fresh from the gloss.

decisions.choice: "lakini mimi, katika BWANA nitashangilia" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the emphatic "I" and the Hebrew order (m1).

decisions.choice: "tôi, tôi sẽ hân hoan" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal repeats the pronoun to keep the Hebrew's emphatic "I" (m1).

decisions.choice: "나, 나는" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal repeats the pronoun to keep the Hebrew's emphatic "I" (m1).

source.text: יְהוִ֤הּאֲדֹנָי֙ חֵילִ֔י וַיָּ֤שֶׂם רַגְלַי֙ כָּֽאַיָּל֔וֹת וְעַ֥ל בָּמוֹתַ֖י יַדְרִכֵ֑נִי לַמְנַצֵּ֖חַ בִּנְגִינוֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh, [the] Lord, [is] my strength, and he makes my feet like the does, and on my high places he makes me tread. To the director, with my stringed instruments.

en.L: {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} my Lord [is] my strength, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes my feet like the does', \q and on my heights {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes me tread. \q For the director: with stringed instruments.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} is my strength; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes my feet as sure as a deer's \q and lets me walk on the heights. \q For the music director. With stringed instruments.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} is my strength. \q He makes me sure-footed like a deer. \q He lets me walk safely high up in the mountains. \q For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments.

es.L: {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}, mi Señor, [es] mi fuerza, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace mis pies como [los] de las ciervas, \q y sobre mis alturas {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me hace andar. \q Al director del coro: con instrumentos de cuerda.
es.B: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} es mi fuerza; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace mis pies tan seguros como los del ciervo \q y me hace andar por las alturas. \q Al director del coro. Con instrumentos de cuerda.
es.R: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} es mi fuerza. \q Me hace caminar seguro como un ciervo. \q Me deja andar a salvo en lo alto de las montañas. \q Para el director de la música. Para tocarse con instrumentos de cuerda.

fr.L: {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}, mon Seigneur, [est] ma force, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rend mes pieds comme [ceux] des biches, \q et sur mes hauteurs {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me fait marcher. \q Au chef de chœur : avec instruments à cordes.
fr.B: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} est ma force ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rend mes pieds aussi sûrs que ceux d’une biche \q et me fait marcher sur les hauteurs. \q Au chef de chœur. Avec instruments à cordes.
fr.R: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} est ma force. \q Il me donne le pied sûr comme une biche. \q Il me fait marcher sans danger tout en haut des montagnes. \q Pour le chef des musiciens. À jouer sur des instruments à cordes.

sw.L: {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} Bwana wangu [ni] nguvu yangu, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} anaifanya miguu yangu kama ya kulungu jike, \q na juu ya mahali pangu pa juu ananifanya nitembee. \q Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya: kwa ala zangu za nyuzi.
sw.B: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ni nguvu yangu; \q anaifanya miguu yangu kuwa imara kama ya ayala \q na kuniwezesha kutembea juu ya vilele. \q Kwa kiongozi wa kwaya. Kwa ala zangu za nyuzi.
sw.R: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ni nguvu yangu. \q Ananifanya niwe na miguu imara kama ya ayala. \q Ananiwezesha kutembea salama juu milimani. \q Kwa kiongozi wa waimbaji. Ipigwe kwa ala za nyuzi.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Chúa tôi, [là] sức mạnh của tôi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm cho chân tôi như [chân] nai cái, \q và trên các nơi cao của tôi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho tôi bước đi. \q Cho người chỉ huy [ban nhạc]: với đàn dây.
vi.B: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} chính là sức mạnh của tôi; \q {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm cho chân tôi vững như chân nai \q và cho tôi bước đi trên các nơi cao. \q Cho nhạc trưởng. Với đàn dây.
vi.R: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban sức mạnh cho tôi. \q Ngài làm cho chân tôi vững vàng như chân nai. \q Ngài cho tôi bước đi an toàn trên núi cao. \q Cho người hướng dẫn ban nhạc. Để chơi bằng đàn dây.

ko.L: {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 나의 주님은 나의 힘이시다. \q 그분께서 내 발을 암사슴들의 [발]처럼 만드시고, \q 나의 높은 곳들을 밟게 하신다. \q 지휘자를 위하여. 현악기에 맞추어.
ko.B: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서는 나의 힘이시다. \q 그분께서 내 발을 사슴의 발처럼 든든하게 하시고 \q 높은 곳을 걷게 하신다. \q 음악 지휘자를 위하여. 현악기에 맞추어.
ko.R: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서는 나에게 힘을 주신다. \q 그분께서는 사슴처럼 내 발을 튼튼하게 하신다. \q 높은 산 위에서도 안전하게 걷게 하신다. \q 찬양 인도자를 위해 현악기로 연주하는 노래.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord: the divine name and the title
decisions.reason: Here the name comes before the title (*'Adonai*), as in Psalm 140:8. The name is then read aloud as "God" so as not to say "Lord" twice.

decisions.choice: my feet like the does', on my heights: the words of Psalm 18:34
decisions.reason: David says the same of God in Psalm 18:34 (2 Samuel 22:34): "making my feet like the does', and on my heights he makes me stand". Habakkuk says "tread" or "walk". The doe is sure-footed on steep, rocky heights; God gives him safety and strength to stand where others would fall. Deuteronomy 32:13 and Isaiah 58:14 speak of riding on the heights of the land.

decisions.choice: For the director: with stringed instruments: a note for the leader of the temple music
decisions.reason: The psalm closes with the kind of note that stands at the head of many psalms (Psalm 4:1): it is for the leader of the music, to be played on stringed instruments. Here it comes at the end, and the Hebrew says "my stringed instruments". It shows that the prayer was used in worship.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord (L); the Lord GOD (B, R); the Psalm 18:34 wording
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 140:8, the name is written GOD so that the two are not read as "Lord Lord"; Balanced and Readable use the familiar order. The lines about the feet and the heights take the published wording of Psalm 18:34 at each level, with "tread" or "walk" for Habakkuk's verb.

decisions.choice: the Psalm 4:1 wording for the note
decisions.reason: The note to the director follows Psalm 4:1 at each level: "For the director: with stringed instruments" (Literal), "For the music director. With stringed instruments" (Balanced), "For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments" (Readable). It stands as the last line of the verse.

decisions.choice: the Spanish Psalm 18:34 wording
decisions.reason: The second and third lines reuse the Spanish of Psalm 18:34 at each level where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: The published Psalm 18:34 words ("mes pieds comme [ceux] des biches", "aussi sûrs que ceux d'une biche", "le pied sûr comme une biche") and the Psalm 4:1 note at each level
decisions.reason: Habakkuk ends with a line of Psalm 18:34 and a psalm's note for the music director; French reuses both published Psalms at each level, changing only "tenir debout" to "marcher" for the Hebrew "tread".

decisions.choice: "MUNGU Bwana wangu" (L); "Bwana MUNGU" (B, R), with the divine_name span on MUNGU
decisions.reason: YHWH followed by Adonai: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, and Balanced and Readable use the set form for "the Lord GOD", "Bwana MUNGU", as the term sheet.

decisions.choice: the Vietnamese wording of Psalm 18:34 for the feet like a deer's, with "bước đi" for "tread", and of Psalm 4:1 for the closing note
decisions.reason: The meaning decisions: the line is Psalm 18:34 and the note is a psalm note; the published Vietnamese is reused where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: "GOD my Lord" is "{{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}, 나의 주님" (L) and "the Lord GOD" "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}" (B, R); the honorific 께서 and 이시다 follow the span, never 은/는
decisions.reason: The term sheet's particle rule: 하나님 ends in a consonant and 야훼 in a vowel, so only particles that read after both stand outside the span. The feet like the does' and the heights reuse the Korean Psalm 18:34 at each level.

decisions.choice: the Spanish Psalm 4:1 wording for the note
decisions.reason: The closing note follows the published Spanish title of Psalm 4 at each level.

decisions.choice: the Psalm 18:34 wording ("kama ya kulungu jike" L, "kama ya ayala" B, R) and the Psalm 4:1 wording for the closing note
decisions.reason: Habakkuk uses the words of Psalm 18:34, and the closing note is a psalm title like Psalm 4:1, so each level reuses the published Swahili of those verses. "Zangu" (my instruments) is kept at L and B, as the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: The closing note reuses the Korean Psalm 4:1 title: "지휘자를 위하여. 현악기에 맞추어." (L), "음악 지휘자를 위하여…" (B), "찬양 인도자를 위해 현악기로 연주하는" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet says; the note is a psalm heading placed at the end.

decisions.choice: "CHÚA, Chúa tôi" (L) / "Chúa là CHÚA" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order of the name and the title; Balanced and Readable use the usual form for "the Lord GOD".
